The test image is unambiguous: it shows the classic bacterial streaming test — a cut tomato stem section placed in a beaker of water with white milky bacterial ooze visibly streaming downward from the cut end. The stem itself shows brown internal discoloration. This is the pathognomonic diagnostic for *Ralstonia solanacearum* (Southern Bacterial Wilt).

The reference image confirms: it shows a longitudinally split tomato stem with brown pith/vascular discoloration, fully consistent with the disease.

The KB description matches exactly: "A white slimy bacterial substance streams from a freshly cut stem base placed in water... The interior stem shows dark or light brown discoloration in the pith area."
